description: We’re a team of three Egyptian high school students interested in space, science, and technology. We enjoy exploring new ideas, solving problems, and turning creative thinking into practical solutions.
summary:
ASTRA is an autonomous, offline-first clinical decision support system designed to safeguard astronaut health during deep-space missions (such as Artemis and Mars transit) where up to 22 minutes of signal latency prevents real-time consultation with Earth-based flight surgeons. Built for non-medical crew members, the application transforms a 60-second daily check-in of wearable vitals, point-of-care blood biomarkers, and guided self-assessments into clear diagnostic predictions and countermeasure protocols.

To eliminate AI medical hallucinations in safety-critical environments, Astralis uses a two-tier hybrid architecture: a deterministic System 1 risk classifier (Laya AI, fine-tuned on 6,000 NASA-parameterized mission logs across 10 physiological attributes) calculates calibrated probabilities for 10 spaceflight conditions—including Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), Space Anemia, Decompression Sickness, and Renal Stone Risk—while a System 2 generative advisor translates active alerts into plain-English explanations and step-by-step NASA countermeasure checklists. Featuring an interactive anatomical dashboard, guided measurement tooltips, and one-click mission presets in a responsive Flutter interface, Astralis empowers astronauts to self-triage silent microgravity hazards before they escalate into mission-threatening emergencies.
details:
Project Details

1. What Does It Do & How Does It Work?

1. Guided 60-Second Assessment & Education Layer:

  • Astronauts input 10 essential physiological, environmental, and psychological attributes organized across three rapid stages:
    • Stage 1 — Essential Vitals (Cardiovascular & Thermal): Resting Heart Rate (heart_rate in bpm), Systolic Blood Pressure (systolic_bp in mmHg), Diastolic Blood Pressure (diastolic_bp in mmHg), Blood Oxygen Saturation (spo2 in %), and Core Body Temperature (body_temp in °C).
    • Stage 2 — Blood & Habitat (Biomarkers & Exposure): Fasting Blood Glucose (blood_glucose(fasting) in mg/dL), Daily Radiation Dose (radiation_dose_daily in mSv/day), and Cabin $CO_2$ Partial Pressure (cabin_co2 in mmHg).
    • Stage 3 — Mental & Sleep (Neuro-Vestibular, Sleep & Readiness): Total Sleep Duration (sleep_hours in hours over the last 24h) and Mood & Cognitive Stress Score (mood_stress_score on a 1–10 scale).
  • Because astronauts are not all medical specialists, every metric features built-in "How & Why" measurement guides explaining proper collection technique in microgravity and why orbital baselines differ from Earth norms.

2. Tier 1 — Deterministic Diagnostic Engine (Random Forest Classifier):

  • Raw numerical inputs are serialized into a 10-feature state vectorand evaluated locally in milliseconds by a custom-trained Random Forest Classifier (scikit-learn).
  • Rather than guessing with generative text, Tier 1 uses ensemble decision-tree bagging to output calibrated probability scores (predict_proba) across 10 physiological states: Healthy, Cardiovascular Deconditioning, Immune/Viral Reactivation, Fatigue/Circadian Disorder, Hypoxia/$CO_2$ Anomaly, Space Anemia, Acute Radiation Stress, Renal Stone Risk, Decompression Sickness, and SANS (Neuro-Ocular Syndrome).

3. Tier 2 — Grounded Countermeasure Advisor & Gamified Bio-Sync:

  • Only conditions crossing the calibrated probability threshold ($P \ge 0.50$) are passed to the Tier 2 advisor (FastAPI backend with AI/local LLM integration).
  • The advisor translates the structured medical flags into plain-English physiological explanations and a 3-step operational protocol (immediate hydration/nutrition intervention, exercise/habitat countermeasure adjustment, and follow-up verification timing), clearly distinguishing between Level 1 Crew Self-Care and Level 2 Flight Surgeon Escalation, while rewarding crew adherence through a gamified Bio-Sync streak and task system.

2. Benefits & Expected Impact

  • Deep-Space Autonomy: Operates completely offline during communication blackouts or high-latency lunar and Martian missions.
  • Zero Medical Hallucinations & Explainable Triage: Strictly separates deterministic tree-based risk classification (System 1 Random Forest) from natural-language guidance (System 2), ensuring clinical reliability and transparent feature importance.
  • Cognitive Offloading & Gamified Engagement: Replaces spreadsheet telemetry and alarm fatigue with color-coded visual triage ribbons, interactive diagnostic wizards, and daily health streaks, allowing fatigued astronauts to grasp their health status in seconds.
  • Terrestrial Spin-Off Value: Directly adaptable to isolated, resource-constrained environments on Earth, including polar research stations, submarines, offshore rigs, and rural telemedicine clinics.

3. Space Agency Data & Resources Used

Because real astronaut medical telemetry is protected under medical privacy regulations, we grounded our diagnostic architecture, feature thresholds, and synthetic dataset generation in official space agency literature and hardware frameworks:

  • NASA Human Research Program (HRP) Evidence Books & Exploration Medical Capability (ExMC): Used to define our 10 target conditions, establish physiological perturbation rules across the "RIDGE" hazards (Radiation, Isolation, Distance, Gravity, Environment), and calibrate two-tier clinical alert thresholds.
  • NASA Crew Health and Performance Integrated Data Architecture (CHP-IDA): Inspired our unified aggregation of disparate habit logs, habitat environmental sensors (cabin_co2, radiation_dose_daily), wearable vitals, and metabolic markersinto a single clinical decision support interface.
  • ISS Point-of-Care & Environmental Monitoring Standards: Selected point-of-care metabolic (blood_glucose(fasting)) and spacecraft life-support/dosimetry indicators (cabin_co2, radiation_dose_daily)that match operational monitoring hardware flown aboard the International Space Station.

4. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Frontend: Flutter & Dart (responsive dark-mode web/desktop terminal featuring custom starfield canvas painter, 3-stage assessment wizard, mission presets, gamified streak/task tracker, and interactive diagnostic dashboard).
  • Machine Learning (System 1): Python and scikit-learn (Random Forest Classifier trained and validated on our 10-attribute physiological & habitat dataset, serialized via joblib/pickle for ultra-fast local CPU inference).
  • Backend & System 2 Advisor: FastAPI (Python), REST API integration with Gemini API and local offline LLM fallback (Ollama / Gemma / Llama).
  • Data Engineering: Python (numpy, pandas) synthetic physiological dataset generator producing 6,000 training logs (60 simulated crew profiles) and 2,000 unseen test logs (20 separate crew profiles) across the 10 core telemetry featureswith zero subject leakage.
  • Design & Presentation: Stitch AI, Figma, and Manus / Gamma AI.

5. Honest Limitations & Next Steps

  • Current Limitation: The Random Forest classification model is trained and validated on parameterized synthetic telemetry rather than de-identified clinical flight records.
  • Next Step 1 (Hardware & Sensor Ingestion): Integrate Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) APIs for automated wearable syncing, spacecraft ECLSS telemetry streaming (for cabin_co2 and radiation_dose_daily), and webcam-based remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) for contactless heart_rate estimation.
  • Next Step 2 (Analog Validation): Validate the software workflow, gamified task adherence, and calibration accuracy in terrestrial space-analog missions (such as NASA HERA or the Mars Desert Research Station).
